sources.note: Version detection matches the dotted prefixes '3.0.' and '3.1.' against the document's openapi field. A document declaring exactly "3.0" or "3.1" with no patch segment is rejected; write "3.0.0" or "3.1.0".

sdk.floorReason: ^1.24.0 is the first range GHSA-w48q-cv73-mx4w considers patched (#140). packages/transports/src/sdk-peer-range.test.ts fails if either declaration drops below it. Until matrix 2.0.0 this file published ^0.5.0 — the line the code had already excluded for that advisory.
sdk.isolation: The SDK is imported by packages/transports only; it is not part of any public API surface.

contract.policy: Changes to this matrix require a semver bump and a release-notes entry. Removing support for a listed version, or narrowing a supported range, is a breaking change and requires a major version bump. Adding a newly supported version is a minor release.
contract.authority: NEITHER file is derived from the other and neither has the greater claim to correctness: both are maintained by hand and must be edited together in the same change. Earlier revisions said the .md was 'the human-readable rendering of it' and that 'the JSON governs' on a disagreement — the first asserted a derivation that was never built, and the second is an arbitrary tie-break presented as authoritative, which misdirects whoever finds a disagreement. If the two disagree, BOTH are suspect and the code decides: check-compatibility-contract.mjs re-derives the machine-comparable values from package.json and package-lock.json on every run. It also compares the two copies, so one being fixed without the other now fails; note that it CANNOT see drift that hits both copies identically, which is exactly how the ^0.5.0 SDK row survived — the re-derivation, not the comparison, is what catches that.
contract.enforcement: PARTIALLY CI-ENFORCED since matrix 2.1.0, widened in 2.2.0. check-compatibility-contract.mjs runs NINE checks and fails the build on any of them: (A) an entry carrying `declared` names no `source`; (B) a `declared` range disagrees with the value at its `source`; (C) a `tested` version disagrees with the lockfile; (D) a `supported` adapter names an entry point this repository does not publish; (E) a machine-comparable value in this file is absent from the .md; (F) a row carrying a `version` declares neither a `source` on its parent nor its own `verifiedBy`; (G) no `supported` row covers the major the lockfile actually installs; (H) a `verifiedBy` names a file that does not exist; (I) this field's own enumeration of those checks disagrees with the checks the guard defines, or with the copy of the same list in the .md. F, G and H arrived in 2.2.0 (#618); I arrived in 2.3.0 (#630). NOTE WHAT I DOES AND DOES NOT CHECK: it compares the LETTER SET and the COUNT stated here against the checks this guard actually defines, and against the same list in docs/compatibility.md. It does NOT read the DESCRIPTIONS — reword what C means and nothing fires. That bound is stated because this field had already gone stale once in exactly the way a description can: it claimed a versioned row naming no source fails the build, which F stopped being true. NOTE WHAT F CHANGED ABOUT ENROLMENT: a row is enrolled by carrying a `version`, not by carrying a `declared`, so a version-bearing row naming only `verifiedBy` passes WITHOUT a `source`. Earlier revisions of this field said a versioned row naming no source fails the build; that is no longer true, and A — which still requires `source` on any entry carrying `declared` — is a narrower claim than it used to read as. What remains UNENFORCED is the expensive half: actually running the test suite against every cell, so a `declared-untested` row is still a statement of expectation. That is Epic #5. Before 2.1.0 this field said 'not a CI-enforced guarantee', which was accurate and was the bound nobody had scheduled the work to lift.
